root_cause.text: In `drivers/media/pci/cx23885/cx23885-alsa.c`, `snd_cx23885_hw_params()` failed to undo the DMA mapping created by `cx23885_alsa_dma_map()` when `cx23885_risc_databuffer()` returned an error, causing a resource leak in the error path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `cx23885_alsa_dma_unmap(chip);` immediately before `goto error;` inside the `if (ret < 0)` block, and the commit message explicitly says “In error path, add cx23885_alsa_dma_unmap() to release the resource acquired by cx23885_alsa_dma_map().”

intent_record.intent_summary: Unmap ALSA DMA resources when RISC databuffer setup fails to avoid leaking DMA mappings on error.
intent_record.what: The error check after cx23885_risc_databuffer() was expanded from a single-line `if (ret < 0) goto error;` into a block that first calls `cx23885_alsa_dma_unmap(chip);` and then jumps to `error`.
intent_record.how: If RISC buffer setup fails, the code now explicitly unmaps the ALSA DMA resources before exiting the function, preventing a resource leak or stale DMA mapping from persisting after an initialization failure.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is enough to evaluate the error path in `snd_cx23885_hw_params()`. The root cause is present: DMA mapping is performed via `cx23885_alsa_dma_map(substream, params);` and then the code calls `ret = cx23885_risc_databuffer(..);`. On failure it returns immediately with `if (ret < 0) return ret;` without undoing the earlier DMA mapping. The only unmap call appears later in the success path: `cx23885_alsa_dma_unmap(substream);`, so the error path leaks the DMA mapping. There is no compensating cleanup before the early return, so the fix is not present in this version.
